newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORDIC SKIING-DAEHLIE DELIGHTS FANS WITH BRILLIANT WIN.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-DAEHLIE DELIGHTS FANS WITH BRILLIANT WIN.

text.p: Bjorn Daehlie delighted his noisy home fans by earning Norway's first gold medal at this year's Nordic skiing world championships with an impressive win in the 10-km, classical race on Monday.

Daehlie, who had to be content with silver in the 30-km freestyle which opened the championships on Friday, lived up to his reputation as the greatest cross-country skier of all time by leaving his rivals helpless on a demanding, bumpy course.
The 29-year-old Norwegian, who had already won six world titles in his career, fell to the snow exhausted at the finish line after giving his all to clock a winning time of 23 minutes 41.80 seconds.
Not even Russian Alexei Prokurorov, who had beaten Daehlie into second place in the 30-km freestyle, could match the pace and he had to settle for second place a huge 27.9 seconds behind.
Finn Mika Myllilae was third, a further 4.5 seconds back, while Vladimir Smirnov of Kazakhstan, the reigning world champion, could do no better than fourth.
Cheered on by some 20,000 partisan supporters waving banners and shaking cowbells, Daehlie was fastest at all the intermediate checkpoints on his way to a much-awaited victory.

"Everybody was screaming for a Norwegian gold medal and that probaby made me go faster," he said after catching his breath. "At one point, I was worried that I might have started too fast but it was okay."
Prokurorov was pleased with his silver medal.

"Second place is fine," the Russian veteran said. "I made a relatively slow start but I was feeling better and better and I was able to take second place. Anyway, Bjorn was too strong for any of us today."
Myllilae, who has scored two World Cup wins this winter, said he had been bitterly disappointed with his 10th place in the 30-km freestyle.

"I was under a lot of pressure because everybody in Finland expected me to win a medal here," he said. "I felt awful after the 30-km and I'm happy with my medal. I was not at 100 per cent today but even if I had been, I would not have won. Bjorn was unbeatable."
Daehlie will go for more in Tuesday's 15-km freestyle pursuit, when he will start with the advantage he built up over his rivals on Monday.
"I must forget this gold medal," he said. "I must not believe that I can win tomorrow (Tuesday) before I get over the line."
But both Prokurorov and Myllilae said they had little hope of preventing the mighty Norwegian from winning again.
"I'll go for it but there's not much I can do against that man," said Myllilae, pointing at Daehlie. "He's from another planet."
